docs.text: Scope, architecture, and validation ¶ Package structure ¶ The distribution is pystac-ext-order ; the import is pystac.extensions.order . The wheel excludes the shared namespace initializer owned by PySTAC. OrderExtension wraps existing metadata dictionaries, so PySTAC's normal serialization preserves changes. It does not submit or monitor orders. The module is generated. Schema-defined changes belong in the source schema and repository generation workflow, rather than manual edits to generated Python. Owners and summaries ¶ Assets and item asset definitions check registration on their owner. Item-owned Assets inherit missing fields from Item properties; explicit null masks an inherited value. Collection-owned Assets do not inherit Collection fields. Collections expose direct metadata and a separate status summary wrapper. Summaries preserve lists, ranges, and JSON Schema dictionaries without computing values from child Items. Validation boundaries ¶ Install pystac[validation] to use validation. OrderExtension.validate() validates the entire Item or Collection against the embedded Order schema with format checking. For Assets and item asset definitions it validates their owner; an unowned object raises pystac.STACError . Invalid documents raise jsonschema.exceptions.ValidationError . This extension-only check does not validate the STAC core schema. Use item.validate() or collection.validate() for core and registered extension validation; that path may retrieve remote schemas. Property assignment, apply() , and to_dict() do not validate the schema. apply() checks field names before mutation. Explicit null is distinct from a missing field, but is not valid for the schema's string fields. Use UTC date-time strings ending in Z for dates, which remain strings throughout serialization. Schema registration and versions ¶ SCHEMA_URI identifies Order v1.1.0. has_extension() checks that exact URI. ext() and summaries() require registration on STAC objects unless add_if_missing=True is supplied. Adding this URI does not migrate older metadata. Owned objects use their owner's registration. An unowned Asset may be wrapped without adding registration, but cannot be validated until it has an owner.

docs.text: Install and build ¶ Install the library ¶ The package declares Python 3.11 or later and PySTAC >=1,<2 . The test matrix covers Python 3.11–3.15. python -m pip install pystac-ext-order "pystac[validation]" python -c "from pystac.extensions.order import OrderExtension; print(OrderExtension.get_schema_uri())" Install from a checkout ¶ git clone https://github.com/Terradue/pystac-ext-order.git cd pystac-ext-order python -m pip install -e . If an existing editable installation predates a packaging change, repeat the editable install in that environment. Preview the documentation ¶ Install the package and documentation tools from the checkout. Use a regular installation for API documentation so the module is available in PySTAC’s shared namespace: python -m pip install . "mkdocs<2" mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]" "pymdown-extensions<12" mkdocs serve The PyMdown upper bound keeps the highlighting API compatible with mkdocstrings 1.0.x. Build with warnings treated as errors: mkdocs build --strict Run repository checks ¶ With Hatch installed, run these commands from the checkout: hatch run dev:check hatch run dev:typecheck hatch run dev:security hatch run test:test

docs.text: Work with Order metadata ¶ Update an Item ¶ Using the Item from the tutorial : order . apply ( status = "succeeded" ) assert order . id == "order-1" # Omitted fields are preserved. order . id = None # Remove order:id. order . clear ( "date" ) # Removal is also available by Python property name. Use set_null("id") only when you deliberately need an explicit JSON null. The Order schema requires strings, so explicit null fails validation. Attach metadata to Assets ¶ asset = pystac . Asset ( href = "https://example.com/data.tif" ) item . add_asset ( "data" , asset ) asset_order = OrderExtension . ext ( asset ) assert asset_order . status == "succeeded" # Falls back to Item metadata. asset_order . status = "pending" assert asset . extra_fields [ "order:status" ] == "pending" assert order . status == "succeeded" asset_order . clear ( "status" ) assert asset_order . status == "succeeded" Registration is checked on the owner. Attach Assets and item asset definitions before using add_if_missing=True . Collection-owned Assets do not inherit Collection fields. Asset validation checks the entire owner, including siblings. Collections and summaries ¶ collection = pystac . Collection ( id = "orders" , description = "Order examples" , extent = pystac . Extent ( pystac . SpatialExtent ([[ - 180 , - 90 , 180 , 90 ]]), pystac . TemporalExtent ([[ None , None ]]), ), ) collection_order = OrderExtension . ext ( collection , add_if_missing = True ) collection_order . status = "pending" summaries = OrderExtension . summaries ( collection ) summaries . status = [ "pending" , "succeeded" ] assert collection . summaries . to_dict ()[ "order:status" ] == [ "pending" , "succeeded" ] summaries . status = None # Remove the summary. For an item asset definition, attach a pystac.ItemAssetDefinition to the Collection's item_assets , then retrieve collection.item_assets["data"] and pass that definition to OrderExtension.ext() . PySTAC copies definitions when assigning the mapping, so retrieve the attached definition before editing it.

docs.text: Order fields ¶ OrderExtension.ext() supports Items, Collections, Assets, and item asset definitions. Catalogs and Links are unsupported. STAC field Python property Value type Notes order:status status str Required on Item properties; also exposed in summaries order:id id str Optional order identifier order:date date str Optional UTC date-time string; use a Z suffix order:expiration_date expiration_date str Deprecated; optional UTC date-time string All four fields are supported on all four targets. The embedded schema accepts arbitrary status strings; the wrapper does not impose an enum. Collection validation accepts its schema's alternatives for top-level fields, Assets, item asset definitions, or summaries. Storage and inheritance ¶ Items and item asset definitions use properties ; Collections and Assets use extra_fields . Wrappers mutate these dictionaries directly. Item-owned Assets fall back to Item properties when a local field is absent. Explicit null masks that fallback. Other targets do not inherit owner metadata. Update semantics ¶ Getters return None for missing values without a fallback, or explicit null. Setters and apply() remove fields assigned None . apply() preserves omitted fields and rejects unknown names with TypeError before changing any fields. clear(name) removes a field and is safe to repeat. set_null(name) stores explicit null, which the string fields reject during validation. clear() and set_null() accept Python property names and raise KeyError for unknown names. Setters do not validate values; call validate() explicitly. Collection summaries ¶ OrderExtension.summaries(collection) exposes only status . It accepts lists, pystac.RangeSummary objects, JSON Schema dictionaries, or None . A dictionary with minimum and maximum is returned as a RangeSummary . Assignments replace the previous representation; None removes it. The helper does not compute summaries from Items and has no apply() method.

docs.text: Create an Order Item ¶ Install the package , then run this example: from datetime import datetime , timezone import pystac from pystac.extensions.order import OrderExtension item = pystac . Item ( id = "example-order" , geometry = None , bbox = None , datetime = datetime ( 2026 , 1 , 1 , tzinfo = timezone . utc ), properties = {}, ) order = OrderExtension . ext ( item , add_if_missing = True ) order . apply ( status = "pending" , id = "order-1" , date = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" ) order . validate () serialized = item . to_dict () assert serialized [ "properties" ][ "order:status" ] == "pending" restored = OrderExtension . ext ( pystac . Item . from_dict ( serialized )) assert restored . id == "order-1" assert restored . date == order . date add_if_missing=True registers the schema URI on the Item. The core Item datetime and order:date are independent values. Dates remain strings. The package stores order metadata; it does not submit or execute orders. to_dict() does not perform validation.
